rejected.title: The rock cycle
card: The rock cycle is the set of processes that turn rock of one type into another type. Any rock can change into any of the three types, and most changes take millions of years.
Surface processes
Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces. Erosion moves the pieces away, and deposition drops them in a new place. Layers of sediment that are buried and cemented become sedimentary rock.
Underground processes
Heat and pressure change buried rock into metamorphic rock without melting it. If the rock gets hot enough to melt, it becomes magma. When magma cools, it forms igneous rock.
Uplift
Uplift pushes rock from deep underground up towards the surface. There it can be weathered, and the cycle goes on.
rejected.remember: Rock keeps changing: it breaks down, is buried, is heated or melted, and is uplifted again.

a.q: A river carries sand and pebbles downstream from a mountain. Which rock cycle process is this?
a.why: Erosion is the process that moves weathered pieces of rock, for example in a river or the wind. Deposition is tempting, but it is when the pieces are dropped, not when they are carried. Weathering breaks the rock up before it is moved.
a.clue: Is the sand being broken, carried or dropped?

b.q: Granite that formed deep underground is uplifted to the surface. Which order of processes could turn it into sedimentary rock?
b.why: The granite must first be broken into pieces, then moved, then dropped in layers that are buried and cemented. The reversed order is tempting, but pieces cannot be moved or dropped before weathering makes them. Melting and cooling would give igneous rock, and heat and pressure would give metamorphic rock.
b.clue: What must happen to solid rock before any pieces can be moved?

b.q: A layer of sandstone is buried deep underground. Heat and pressure change it, but it does not melt. What does it become, and which process is this?
opts: Metamorphic rock, by heat and pressure
Igneous rock, by melting and cooling
Sedimentary rock, by burial and cementing
Metamorphic rock, by weathering and erosion
b.why: Heat and pressure that change rock without melting it make metamorphic rock. Igneous rock is tempting, but it needs the rock to melt first. Weathering and erosion break rock down at the surface and do not change it underground.
b.clue: The card says the rock does not melt.

b.best: Metamorphic rock, by heat and pressure
